definition: Indict means to formally charge someone with a crime, usually after a grand jury or prosecutor reviews the evidence.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word indict. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know indict should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: After three days of hearing that evidence, the grand jury voted to indict the city councilman on bribery charges.
Anyone can accuse a neighbor of wrongdoing; to indict someone, a grand jury or prosecutor must bring a formal criminal charge.
An indicted person still awaits trial and may go free; to convict them, a court must actually find them guilty.

To charge someone is to formally accuse them of a specific crime — the general word for what prosecutors do when the paperwork is filed. To indict is to charge by a particular route: a grand jury or prosecutor reviews the evidence and hands the formal accusation down.

To prosecute someone is to conduct the case against them — building evidence, arguing at trial, seeking a conviction over months. To indict them is a single, earlier step: the formal handing down of the criminal charge that a prosecution then pursues.

To arraign someone is to call them into court to answer a charge that already exists — the defendant stands before a judge and enters a plea. To indict them is to create that charge in the first place; arraignment comes next down the line.

Indict means to formally charge someone with a crime, usually after a grand jury or prosecutor reviews the evidence.
Federal prosecutors moved to indict the pharmacist for billing the insurance program for prescriptions that were never filled.
The prosecutors are taking the formal legal step of charging the pharmacist with a specific crime — not merely suspecting him — which is exactly what indict means.
Indict is a courtroom word with a trick pronunciation: the c is silent (in-DITE).
It names the formal legal step of charging someone with a crime — a grand jury indicts.
Keep it distinct from implicate (also taught in this unit): evidence implicates a person by suggesting involvement, but only a formal charge indicts them.
Someone can be implicated for years without ever being indicted.
